transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. It's nice to meet you. Thank you for taking the time to see me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your day. 

Um, I'm here because... well, I guess my family thought it would be a good idea for me to talk to someone. It's just... I've been under a lot of stress lately at my apartment. It's a bit embarrassing to talk about, honestly, because I know how it might sound. But for months now, the property manager and, well, certain people in the building, they've been doing things. Just little things, you know? Like misdelivered mail, and these timed noises in the walls right when I'm trying to sleep. And sometimes neighbors will make these little comments that just... they feel very pointed. 

I really try not to make a fuss, I do. But it feels like they're trying to pressure me out of the apartment. They've shown me paperwork and tried to explain it all away as coincidences, but... well, I can see the pattern, you know? I'm not crazy, I promise. It's just very overwhelming. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.

Aside from the stress about your apartment, have you noticed any periods where your mood was significantly different from your usual self—either feeling unusually high, energetic, and needing little sleep, or feeling very low, hopeless, and losing interest in things?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I mean, obviously the situation at the building has made me a bit tired—just from the interrupted sleep, which I think is a pretty normal reaction, right? But I've never had times where I felt, um, unusually high or energetic like you mentioned. 

And I'm definitely not hopeless. I still really enjoy my day-to-day life. I'm a management analyst, actually, and I still keep up with all my usual projects and routines. I've always been a very steady person, emotionally speaking. I try very hard to keep an even keel, so to speak. 

I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or noises that other people around you couldn't hear, separate from the noises you believe your neighbors are intentionally making?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely nothing like that. I mean, the sounds from the neighbors, the tapping and the thuds, those are... well, they're actual, physical noises. Anyone could hear them if they were sitting right there in the living room with me at the right time. 

But as for voices, or, um, sounds that aren't really there? No, never. I've always had a very firm grip on reality. I know sometimes people can experience things like that when they're unwell, but I promise you, my mind is completely sound. I'm a very logical person. 

I hope that reassures you? I just really want to be clear that I'm not... you know, imagining things out of thin air. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
How long have you been noticing these things happening with your neighbors and property manager—has it been going on continuously for a few weeks, or longer, like several months or more?

Well, um... it's been a little while now. I really didn't want to make a big deal out of it at first, you know? I kept thinking, or hoping rather, that it would just resolve itself if I kept my head down and stayed polite. But, I suppose it's been going on continuously for about... oh, almost eleven months now. It started just shortly after I moved into the new apartment. 

I probably should have spoken to someone sooner, but I really hate being a bother or seeming like a difficult tenant. Is eleven months... does that timeframe make sense to you? I hope I'm being helpful. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you the exact details you need.

Do you have any medical conditions—like thyroid problems, seizures, head injuries, or substance use (including alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications)—that started or changed around the time these beliefs began?

No, no medical conditions like that. I've always been very diligent about my health, actually. I make sure to go to my annual checkups and, well, my doctor always says I'm in great shape for my age. 

I don't have any thyroid issues or history of seizures, and I've certainly never had a head injury. As for, um, substances... I don't use any recreational drugs at all, and I only have a glass of wine on very rare occasions, like a holiday or a special dinner. I'm not taking any new medications either. 

I've always tried to be very responsible and take good care of myself, so there hasn't been anything physical that could be causing... well, any confusion or anything like that. Does that answer your question? I just want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you all the right context.
Aside from the stress this situation causes, has it affected your relationships with friends or family, or your ability to take care of yourself day-to-day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, it is stressful, certainly, but I really try my best not to let it burden my friends or family. I always try to be a good friend and keep things pleasant when we speak. 

And as for taking care of myself... well, I'm doing just fine. Truly. When I'm not having to, um, deal with the whole apartment situation, everything else is very normal. I still manage all my own finances—I've always been very meticulous with numbers, given my background in analysis. I cook for myself every day, I make sure to keep all my appointments... and I can still discuss my consulting work, or even my painting, in a very clear, organized way. 

I haven't let things fall apart, I promise. I hope that shows you I'm still managing things quite well? I just really want you to know that I'm fully capable of handling my day-to-day life. Does that help give you a better picture of how I'm doing?
